name: Workflowy
tagline: An infinitely nested bulleted list you can zoom into, used as a notes app, task manager and second brain.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core of Workflowy is a nested list with zoom, collapse, search and fast keyboard editing, and that is genuinely one-sitting work for a coding agent. What takes longer is everything around it: multi-device sync that never eats a keystroke, real mobile apps, offline conflict handling, shared links, mirrors and backlinks. A local build is fine for one person on one machine and starts to hurt the moment you want the same outline on a phone at the grocery store. The other half of the product is invisible polish: cursor behavior on indent, undo across moves, paste of multi-level text, and not choking on a fifty thousand node document. Buildable, but you will spend your weekend on the boring correctness instead of the fun part.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app storing one big outline in SQLite, with infinite nesting, zoom into any bullet, collapse, tags, full text search and Workflowy-style keyboard shortcuts.
requirements: a machine you leave running if you want to reach it from a phone on the same network
a backup habit, because it is one SQLite file
whatYouLose: Real iOS and Android apps with offline editing and sync
Conflict-free sync across devices, which is the actual hard engineering
Shared and published outlines, plus collaborator editing
Mirrors, backlinks, boards and the other power features layered on top of the outline
Someone else worrying about your data surviving a disk failure
moatNotes: Fifteen years of keyboard edge cases and a sync engine that people trust with their entire task list. Neither shows up in a feature comparison.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because an outliner is only useful if it is everywhere and instant, and Workflowy has quietly solved the parts that are unglamorous: sync that does not lose a bullet, a mobile app that opens fast, undo that behaves after you drag a subtree three levels up. People also have a decade of nested life in there, which makes any migration feel like moving house. The paid tier mostly buys unlimited bullets and backups, which is a small price against the risk of your own build corrupting the tree at 11pm.
notes: The outline is easy, the sync engine is the product.
prompt:
Build a local-first infinite outliner, a personal Workflowy replacement, in an empty folder.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Vite + React + TypeScript for the client.
- Express (Node 20+) + better-sqlite3 for the server.
- One SQLite file at ./data/outline.db, created on first run.
- No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry, no analytics. Single user.

Data model:
- nodes table: id (uuid), parent_id (nullable), position (float for cheap reordering), text, collapsed (bool), completed (bool), note (nullable), created_at, updated_at.
- One implicit root. Arbitrary nesting depth.

Server:
- GET /api/tree returns the whole outline as nested JSON.
- POST /api/ops accepts a batch of operations: create, update_text, indent, outdent, move, toggle_collapse, toggle_complete, delete_subtree. Apply in a transaction.
- GET /api/search?q= does substring and #tag matching, returns matching nodes with their ancestor breadcrumb.
- GET /api/export returns the outline as indented Markdown. POST /api/import accepts indented Markdown and appends it.

Client behavior, this is the part that matters:
- Single editable outline view. Enter creates a sibling, Tab indents, Shift+Tab outdents, Backspace at start of an empty bullet deletes and merges upward.
- Cmd/Ctrl+Up and Down move the current subtree. Cmd/Ctrl+Enter toggles complete. Click a bullet to zoom into it, with a breadcrumb trail back to root.
- Arrow keys move between bullets and preserve caret column. Local undo stack for at least 50 operations, including moves and deletes.
- Pasting multi-line indented text creates the matching subtree instead of one giant bullet.
- Optimistic local state, debounced batched writes to /api/ops, so typing never waits on the network.
- #tags are highlighted and clickable, filtering to matching bullets.
- Virtualize rendering so a 20,000 node outline stays smooth.

Out of scope: mobile apps, real-time collaboration, sharing links, mirrors, backlinks, boards, any auth.

Also write: a seed script that generates a 20,000 node outline for performance testing, a nightly cron-friendly script that copies the SQLite file into ./backups with a timestamp, and a README with run instructions and a blunt note that this is single-device and the database file is the only copy of the data.
